title: Where to go after Yerin Baek’s “0310”
description: The writing process behind tellusboutyourself offers a route from “0310” to her next album.

blocks.text: Yerin Baek’s name keeps coming up in the credits for “0310”. She wrote the music and lyrics, arranged it with Cloud, and played electric guitar alongside jonny and Cloud. Released on Every letter I sent you. in December 2019, the song already finds her involved well beyond the vocal.
That is a useful starting point for her next album, tellusboutyourself, released on 10 December 2020. What changed was partly the way a song began.

Speaking to Franchesca Judine Basbas for Bandwagon at the time of its release, Baek described the album as a collection of songs she wanted to perform on stage. For “0415”, she had a specific wish: to hear her voice on a deep house track. A setting for the voice could be part of the idea from the outset.

The experiments had begun before “0310” came out. In Daichi Yamamoto’s interview with Baek and Cloud for POCLANOS, she recalled taking a few MIDI lessons from Cloud in early 2019. She began making sketches herself and sent him starting versions of 13 of the next album’s 14 songs. Some of her own beats and keyboard parts made it into the finished work.

She described reversing her usual order. For the first album, she had played piano or guitar while writing melody and lyrics together. This time she found a beat she liked, set the tempo, played keyboard, then added melody and words. The sketches helped Cloud understand the style she had in mind when arranging.

Baek later gave two more specific entry points in an interview with Alyssa Bailey for ELLE: “HOMESWEETHOME” and “Bubbles&Mushrooms”. She named these as the songs on which she had pushed herself furthest, describing her attempts at house and 2-step. She also credited a new producer joining the team with helping her try music outside her previous habits.
Baek was already a co-arranger on “0310”. Her sketches gave that collaboration a more concrete starting point: Cloud could hear her intentions before arranging.
For a next song, try “0415” with her original wish in mind: she wanted to place her voice in deep house. Then move to “HOMESWEETHOME” or “Bubbles&Mushrooms”, the experiments she singled out herself.

editorial.reason: The exact draft answers its reader question with a useful connection between Baek’s existing creative role, her changed composing process and three justified next listens. Comparison with the opened originals found no material imitation or invented experience. This is editorial approval of the supplied draft only.
editorial.contribution: The credits establish that Baek already composed and co-arranged “0310”; the interviews explain how sketches changed her collaboration with Cloud. Combining that distinction with her own song-specific accounts produces a practical listening route without claiming firsthand sonic analysis.
comparisons: The draft applies the specificity of [Nick Caceres’s Parannoul interview](https://nicholasc2002271.wixsite.com/nickc/copy-of-interview-w-matt-cruz-from-lr): a working decision matters more than a generic growth narrative. It borrows no distinctive questions, personal experiences, imagery or narrative sequence.

Against [Basbas’s Bandwagon article](https://www.bandwagon.asia/articles/yerin-baek-shares-a-new-side-and-stories-of-growth-in-her-latest-album-tellusboutyourself-korea-blue-vinyl-kpop-comeback-interview-december-2020), the draft retains attributed intentions but avoids the correspondence metaphor and transformation framing. The stage-intention-to-0415 sequence follows relevant evidence; the credits and composing-process connection supply a different argument.

The two process paragraphs condense separate answers in the [POCLANOS interview](https://poclanos.com/interview/yerinbaek/). Their procedural order is necessary to explain the change, rather than an appropriated narrative device. The draft preserves the distinction between sketches and finished production.

The [ELLE interview](https://www.elle.com/culture/music/a35755652/yerin-baek-tellusboutyourself-interview/) supplies the two experimental selections. Attribution remains explicit, and the draft does not assign house and 2-step individually to the songs or present the artist’s account as our hearing.

Using the dossier’s whole-paragraph counting method, source contributions are approximately 189 words for POCLANOS process, including title, deck and heading; 91 for Bandwagon; 90 for ELLE; and 74 for the credits. These fit the stated 200/100-word limits. No lyrics or substantive direct quotations are reproduced.

Compared with the supplied sunwoojunga story, this opening establishes creative credits rather than reconstructing a personal incident. Its ending offers a listening sequence rather than a broader emotional synthesis. No repetitive opening or ending was found.

The short album-transition paragraph supplies necessary chronology. The penultimate paragraph repeats earlier evidence but earns its place by connecting the credits to the sketches. The concrete credits, dates, workflow and named selections keep the article from becoming interchangeable artist praise. No listening, interview attendance or personal reaction is invented.
